gaps.sentence: If plants ___ enough light, their leaves turn yellow.
gaps.hint: a general truth in the if-clause
gaps.explanation: Zero conditionals state general truths with the present simple in both clauses: do not get.

gaps.sentence: If you order before midnight, delivery ___ nothing.
gaps.hint: result clause of a first conditional
gaps.explanation: The result of a real future condition takes 'will': will cost.

gaps.sentence: If people ___ less time on their phones, they would read more.
gaps.explanation: An unreal present habit takes the past simple in the if-clause: spent.

gaps.sentence: As long as you ___ the rules, you will have no problems here.
gaps.hint: as long as states the condition
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition and takes the present simple: follow.

gaps.sentence: If we ___ tickets today, they will cost half the price.
gaps.explanation: The condition is present simple; only the result clause uses 'will': book.

gaps.sentence: Would you ___ me if I told you a secret?
gaps.hint: would plus infinitive in result clause
gaps.explanation: The result clause of a second conditional uses 'would' plus the infinitive: forgive.

gaps.sentence: Unless something urgent ___, I will be at my desk all morning.
gaps.hint: unless introduces the exception, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the exception to the plan and takes the present simple: comes up.

gaps.sentence: If dogs ___ wings, they would fly.
gaps.hint: an impossible present, past simple if-clause
gaps.explanation: Impossible present conditions still take the past simple after 'if': had.
